extra.message: User-supplied 'search' query parameter from request.args is concatenated directly into a SQL string via an f-string and passed to cursor.execute(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. search=' OR 1=1 --) to read or modify the database. user_id is also interpolated unsafely even though it originates from a parameterized lookup.

The 'search_query' value rendered into the input's value attribute uses the | safe filter, disabling Jinja2's auto-escaping. The value comes from request.args.get('search', '') in the dashboard route, so an attacker can craft a URL containing arbitrary HTML/JavaScript which will execute in the victim's browser (reflected XSS).

The user.country field is rendered with the | safe filter, disabling Jinja2's auto-escaping. Because the country value comes from user-controlled input stored in the database, an attacker can register a user with malicious HTML/JavaScript in the country field and execute arbitrary scripts when any user views that profile (stored XSS).

In the dashboard template's JavaScript, user-supplied 'comment' is concatenated directly into HTML via $commentList.append('
  • ' + comment + '
    • ') without sanitization, enabling DOM-based XSS. While comments are client-only here, the pattern is unsafe.

SECRET_KEY is hardcoded as 'just_another_secret' in source code. This same secret is used for Flask session signing and for signing/verifying JWT tokens in the API. Attackers with source access (e.g., open-source repo, leaked repo) can forge sessions and JWTs to impersonate any user, including admins.

Config.DEBUG is set to True, and run.py launches the Flask app with debug=debug_mode. Running Flask/Werkzeug in debug mode exposes an interactive debugger PIN-protected console that, if PIN-guessing succeeds or PIN is leaked, allows arbitrary code execution (RCE) on the server.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY is set to False. This allows client-side JavaScript (e.g., via XSS) to read the session cookie, enabling session hijacking/account takeover.

The custom_hash function uses unsalted MD5 for password hashing. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsalted hashes are vulnerable to rainbow-table attacks. Passwords stored in the database (see db/create_dummy_data.py hash_password) can be rapidly cracked.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: The hash_password function used to seed user accounts uses unsalted MD5, reinforcing the weak password hashing pattern in server/routes.py custom_hash. Same credentials/weaknesses apply.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: The UserDelete.delete() handler has its @token_required decorator commented out, so the /api/v1/delete-user/<user_id> endpoint is fully unauthenticated and unauthorized. Any unauthenticated attacker can DELETE arbitrary users from the database (Broken Function Level Authorization).

The /api/v1/profile endpoint allows any unauthenticated caller to query profile details (including email, role, permissions, team) for any user_id via the user_id query parameter. The @token_required decorator is commented out. This is a Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR) vulnerability leading to information disclosure.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The /api/v1/update_picture endpoint fetches an arbitrary URL provided by the user via requests.get(picture_url) without any validation, allowlist, or DNS rebinding protection. An attacker can target internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (e.g., http://169.254.169.254/), or local files (file:// schemes may also be reachable depending on transport). This is a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability.

The /api/v1/update_picture endpoint accepts POST requests without any authentication or authorization check (no @token_required). Any unauthenticated attacker can update arbitrary users' profile pictures (SSRF + missing auth combined).

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The /update_profile endpoint allows any authenticated user to set their own 'role' and 'permissions' fields via request.form. The 'if role not in request.form' check is trivially bypassed by including the field. This is a Broken Object Property Level Authorization (BOPLA) vulnerability enabling vertical privilege escalation (any user can become 'admin' with 'all' permissions).

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The upload_file endpoint uses file.filename directly without sanitization in os.path.join(UPLOAD_FOLDER, filename). If filename is an absolute path (e.g. /tmp/x or ../../../etc/cron.d/payload), os.path.join discards earlier components and the file is written to an arbitrary location. Werkzeug's FileStorage.filename is not sanitized by default; secure_filename() must be applied.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The upload_file endpoint accepts any file type and content with no validation of extension, MIME type, or file content. Users can upload executables/scripts (e.g. .php, .html, .exe), which combined with the /uploads/<filename> and /download/<filename> routes can be used to distribute malware or host client-side attacks.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: The /uploads/profile_pictures/<filename> endpoint serves profile pictures without any authentication check, while the equivalent /uploads/<filename> endpoint requires login. This bypasses authentication for the profile picture resource, exposing user-specific data to unauthenticated users (information disclosure / missing authentication).

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: All state-changing endpoints (/login, /signup, /update_profile, /upload, /delete/<filename>, /logout) accept POST requests without CSRF tokens. The Flask app does not enable CSRFProtect or any equivalent protection. An attacker can craft a malicious site that submits forms to perform actions on behalf of authenticated users (CSRF).
Database error messages are printed to stdout via print('Error inserting user:', e) on exceptions. Combined with DEBUG=True this can leak internal SQL/details to logs. Sensitive data exposure risk.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The /api/v1/update-profile endpoint relies solely on the Flask session for authentication (no @token_required or signature validation). API clients (including those not using a browser cookie store) will appear unauthenticated and updates will fail; meanwhile clients that share the session cookie can update other users' profiles if user_id in the request body differs (only partially enforced by the user_id != session_user_id check, which is itself bypassable if data['user_id'] is omitted or matches session).

The token_required decorator uses a bare 'except:' clause that catches all exceptions, including KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit. While not directly exploitable, it can mask serious errors and combined with jwt.decode using a weak hardcoded SECRET_KEY (HS256) allows JWT forgery by anyone with source access.
